facts.statement: IFSC aircraft leasing structure: foreign lessor → IFSC SPV → Indian airline lessee; royalty and interest paid to the non-resident lessor are exempt under Section 10(4F); income on disposal of shares of an aircraft-leasing IFSC unit is eligible for the Section 10(4H) tax holiday; customs duty and GST apply on forward charge for aircraft leased to Indian operators.

Ship leasing in IFSC uses operating-lease and financial-lease structures; Budget 2025 proposed a capital-gains exemption on equity shares of ship-leasing IFSC entities and a dividend exemption between IFSC ship-leasing units.

Leasing trajectory: FY25 - 32 aircraft lessors with 242 aviation assets leased and 24 ship lessors with 18 ships; December-2025 - aviation assets 370 (196 aircraft, 89 engines, 85 APUs) and ships leased 34; IBU financing of aircraft leasing USD 614.85 million and ship leasing USD 71.1 million; September-2025 - aviation assets 303, ships 28, aircraft financing USD 257.17 million.
facts.detail: Module-era baseline (PwC): 30+ aircraft lessors and 158+ assets including Air India A-350s; 12 ship lessors with 4 ships.

facts.statement: The Expert Committee on the Global Commodity Trading Hub (May 2024), chaired by Rajeev Kher (former Commerce Secretary) with 23 members including ONGC, IOCL, NMDC, Trafigura, JP Morgan, Olam, Tata Steel, Reliance and StoneX, was tasked to position GIFT IFSC as a global commodity trading hub covering physical trade, merchanting trade, and OTC and exchange-traded derivatives.
facts.detail: Priority commodities: metals (precious/base/rare earth), energy and hydrocarbons, and agricultural products. Reference hubs: Switzerland, Singapore, London, Chicago, Dubai, Shanghai, Rotterdam. The committee report was published 1 August 2025.

facts.statement: Under IFSC banking directions, metals and commodities trading by IBUs is reported in the Office of Administrator and SEZ section of bulletins; OTC derivatives on gold and silver were enabled as an FY2025 initiative alongside the bullion exchange.

The Expert Committee on Asset Tokenisation (constituted September 2023) consulted in February 2025 with scope limited to real-world assets (not crypto, CBDC or NFTs): securities (funds, bonds, stocks), payments, deposits, bills receivable, bullion, commodities, intellectual property and commercial real estate; estimated savings of USD 15-20 billion annually in global infrastructure operational costs and over USD 100 billion annually freed via DLT collateral management; comments closed 20 March 2025; seven regulatory intents were defined.
